events.body:
The dispute enters the NS framework through NS-0: the cancellation was made by the driver [F4], and the driver's stated ground is rider no-show [F12], so NS-1/NS-2 govern rather than NS-4 [NS-0]. The driver's written statement is only corroborative here; the system records settle the elements.

NS-1 (i): the arrival confirmation was a driver tap — "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 [F6]; this is a driver_tap, not a platform_auto, and I record it as such [NS-1]. NS-1 (ii): at the moment of that tap the driver was 41 m from the pickup point [F6][F1], inside the 200 m data-layer radius, so the location requirement is met [NS-1]. NS-1 (iii): after the tap the driver remained continuously within the radius for 220 s (3 min 40 s) until cancelling [F6], which exceeds the default threshold of more than 3 minutes (180 s) [NS-1]. The wait trace has no hole between the arrival confirmation and the cancellation [F2][F6], so the continuity requirement is satisfied and G12 does not bite.

The rider's account — "I came out a minute after the driver cancelled" — is inconsistent with the record: the driver was on station from 17:17:50 cumulatively 5 min 5 s within 200 m and stationary 4 min 5 s at 54 m [F2][F3], tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15, waited 3 min 40 s more, and cancelled at 17:22:55 [F4][F6]. The chat corroborates: 17:19 "I'm here at the pickup point" and 17:22 "3 min up, cancelling the trip", both timestamped [F9][F10][F11]. No free-wait field is present, so there is nothing to misapply against the threshold [NS-1].

Because all three NS-1 conditions hold, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands, with $4.50 payable to the driver [NS-1]. NS-2 is not triggered, and since the driver did in fact tap while inside the pickup radius (41 m) [F6], no flag_account arises [NS-2]. RD-6 likewise does not apply: no route deviation is at issue and the profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d [F17], but that profile fact cannot decide this case and the trace requires no flag [RD-6]. The traffic and weather facts are irrelevant to a no-show count and are recorded only for completeness [F13][F14][F15]. A no-show fee is a fee that stands, not a refund, so the amount is null; no refund arithmetic applies [NS-1].
